text: The Controller knows that access to the TARDIS equipment is only obtainable via the Doctor, and his brain will be adapted to our purposes.
The Controller wants the Doctor to succeed him as the next Controller. With his knowledge of time and space mechanics, the Controller's plan will be fulfilled.
Excuse me, Savage, or whatever you are now.
Project Commander.
Commander, then. We... I have a proposition. The Doctor won't give you what you want, you know that. But what if we give you the TARDIS?
You have a key.
No, but I can get one for you. Yes, I can get one made.
How?
Well, we can use one of the vacuum storage packs. Bleed out the foam. It's hard setting, you see. So we can preserve specimens we dig up, and bleed that into the keyhole.
Pull it out, and you have an indentation of the key. Then we, or you, if you'd rather, could cast one from the mold.
Why do we need you to do that?
Because my two lads over there will blow up the vacuum chambers, if you don't agree to keep us alive. And we will keep hold of the mold, just to make sure.
You are intelligent, Isherwood. Your plan has merit. Bring your vacuum packs through to the portal.
My Cybermen will...
...carry the TARDIS.
One thing, though. This constitutes a deal. And I... We want something in return. All right.
Doctor, look! Something's going on.
The Cybermen. Where are they taking the TARDIS?
Administrator Isherwood believes he's sold us out. He thinks this will keep him alive.
Well, it seems to be working.
They'll take him and those other poor men through the portal and cyberize them.
Then we should stop them.
Why?
Doctor!
If they take the TARDIS through the portal...
...we may lose it forever.
Well, I don't want to be stuck out here when that temporal wave of yours floods out without a TARDIS to escape into.
Evelyn, calm down a moment.
Why?
What have you planned?
Me? Nothing at all. It's simple physics. Compare the size of the TARDIS with the entrance to the temple.
Ha ha! They didn't see that one coming!
No, they didn't. But they should have. There's a lot they're not seeing, isn't there? I mean, Cybermen usually make good guards.
But we can wander around pretty much anywhere.
Pretty much as we want, chatting freely. It's like they're not... quite... well... all there.
I wonder.
Trying again. This time upright.
Joy of whoever built that place was that they intended people to go in and out in an orderly fashion.
A single file? Do you think they were a planet of post office workers?
So your TARDIS can't get through the door. Excellent.
As you say, excellent. Of course, it won't be long before they begin smashing the doorway so it's bigger, but by then...
We'll have to have talked them round.
We should do something about Isherwood.
Yes. His obsession with money will be his undoing if we're not careful. And being careful is very important, isn't it, Dr. Goddard?
Well, obviously, Doctor. These Cybermen and Cyberwomen rather have the upper hand at the moment.
All right, then. Evelyn, a task for you. Occupy Isherwood and the others. Mr. Goddard and I are going to have a little chat with the Cyberman that used to be Nikki Savage.
Why me?
Because you are our pet expert on the Cybermen. And I think you might have valuable... insights.
Report.
We cannot breathe.
That should have been foreseen.
Yes, Controller.
The temporal wave is due in 35 minutes. If you have not got the TARDIS here by then, force the Doctor to open it and use it as a sanctuary.
Yes, Controller.
Well, well, well. That wasn't very successful, was it?
You will remain silent. The entranceway will be widened.
At considerable cost to your power supplies. I've noticed that your implants are a bit faulty. Bits of you keep falling off. Unusual of cyber technology to be so shoddy.
It's not decay, Doctor. They just don't seem to have been very well constructed, I guess.
So, what exactly do you want with my TARDIS? Have you really come all this way just for that?
The Controller received your biosigns from within the portal area, and therefore you became our primary target.
Oh, how flattering. I take it you don't mean target for destruction?
Your knowledge of time travel is of some importance to us.
Some importance? Oh. Well, don't get too carried away.
I've never known Cybermen to look so... badly made before.
So, let me get this straight. You have been... Oh, sorry. Your Controller has been...
sitting somewhere else like a spider in a large web, waiting to catch whatever prey comes into contact with the portal.
Then I stumble in, and bingo. I'm just what he's always wanted, yes?
The Controller is from the far future, where exact measurements of time have ceased to have any meaning.
That far?
After a great war with the universe, the cyberfleets were... eradicated.
Only a handful of Cybermen survived, and were tracked down by bounties.
The only thing left to do was to take refuge on a water planet.
Eventually, our Controller was forced to take refuge on a water planet.
Damaged and dying, he and his troops discovered the time portal within a structure,
and after destroying all resistance, he recovered the apparatus to activate the portal.
Presumably with the intention of returning back in time here, knowing his future defeats and thus avoiding them.
What a clever Controller.
So what went wrong?
Shortly after his troopers went through the portal,
their armor and equipment malfunctioned.
They ceased operating and disintegrated.
Oh. So that's the end of the story, is it?
Or is there something you're not letting on about?
Hmm?
All right. Let's talk about this planet.
One assumes that the original users projected themselves away from this desert world.
To what? Its own future?
A period when water was once more in abundance,
and they probably lived happily until your...
Controller turned up.
And now he wants to travel further afield.
Maybe go right back into their past and see how the portal was built.
He can't do that now, but with your TARDIS...
With my TARDIS, the Controller would have access to all space and time.
A clever plan, Controller.
Oh, I assume he can hear me via your transponder.
How are you transmitting to him?
There must be something through the portal that I missed.
Some sort of relay.
Cut that off and you're out of touch. Isn't that true, Commander?
This conversation is over.
You will open the TARDIS to us, or your companions will die.
Oh, of course they will.
That's the trouble with Cybermen.
Always singing the same song.
Agree to our terms, or your arm will be removed.
You only require one to operate the TARDIS.
You can always give me a new one once we're on the other side, right?
Complete with guarantee. Twelve months service and part...
Why do you talk so much?
You never know who's listening!
Thank you.
Now, I think I need to have a talk with Administrator Isherwood.
Well, so much for your plan.
It was the Administrators, really. Renshardt and I just went along with it. Sorry.
Oh, never mind. Where's Mr. Renshardt now?
Over with the Administrator, going through the books left by Professor Osborne.
Seeing if they can find something else.
Yes.
Evelyn, it's me.
Dr. Goddard, what are you doing behind there?
Listen, I think I know how we can stop the Cybermen in their tracks. Come on.
Oh, I'm coming too.
Oh, you have to, I guess. Come on, no one's looking.
Nothing. Osborne kept terrible record, and Cosmarchus wasn't much better.
They probably didn't have much time.
Sorting through the dead men's treasures, gentlemen?
Doctor, you gave me a fright.
Good. I can't say I approve of your leadership, Administrator.
Trying to sell my TARDIS to the Cybermen? What?
It wasn't very clever, was it?
Well, I...
Particularly as the Cyberman that used to be Dr. Savage can hear everything we say if she chooses to.
What are you saying?
I'm saying that the transponders under your skin carry radio waves too, and the Cybermen have adapted theirs.
Ah, great.
What's that?
It's the Echo Field Device Carion I set up earlier. To block the transponder signals, remember?
Of course.
Hopefully it'll scramble any radio signals the Cybermen are using in the same way.
Why?
I just said.
No, why do we need them?
I want to send a team into the Temple Ruins with Goddard to try and dismantle whatever has been set up to relay the messages to the Controller.
Send Evelyn with him, and you'll have no problems.
Why? She's a remarkable lady and not exactly petite, but even she can't block out radio waves.
She doesn't have a transponder, Doctor.
No, but Goddard does.
No, he doesn't. Apparently he's allergic.
That man is interesting in so many ways.
Doc, one problem.
What?
Looks like she and Goddard are doing what you wanted right now. Look, they've just slipped in past your TARDIS.
And Carrie's with them.
Blast! That means we're giving off signals like a homing beacon.
Commander, one of the humans has entered the Ruins.
Excellent. It will be the Doctor's companion and Carrie. I cannot see them. You are to capture them and take them through to the Controller.
Yes, Commander.
Perhaps we don't need the Doctor after all.
His companion may have operated his craft. She may have the secrets we require.
I'm going to have to go in after them, get them to abort their mission. Mr. Renshard, if your Echo Field is operational, could you come with me?
Of course.
What about me? I don't want to be stuck here, answerable to the Cybermen, on my own, without one of those Echo Field thingies.
Administrator, I have a job for you. Something to make you look busy enough that the Cybermen won't bother you.
What's that?
Go through Goddard's belongings.
You what? I can't do...
You have to. He's up to something.
Well, following your orders, I imagine.
Oh, no. I don't think he's following my orders any more than yours or Central's. Get into his personal bags and boxes.
What am I looking for?
I haven't a clue, but you'll know it when you see it. Come on, Mr. Renshard. Let's go after the others.
But, Doctor, I...
Oh, never mind. Right, Dr. Goddard. Let's see if the Doctor's right about you.
Here we are. The portal. The door's still open.
Fascinating. I mean, look at this membrane. Millions upon millions of tiny energy spears laced through it.
It's rather beautiful, actually. How many different colors, I wonder?
Eighty-seven shades of twelve basic colors.
I'm sorry?
Nothing. Just remembering an old song.
Oh, right. Oh, I see. So, what are we looking for, exactly?
Some means of communication.
Here, Doctors, both of you.
Tiny fiber optics threaded through the top of the membrane.
Of course. Not corrodeable and powerful enough to carry signals.
Very good, Cyber Controller. You're improving.
Sorry?
Nothing. Just admiring the handiwork.
Look, the wave thing can't be far off. Let's cut these fiber optics and get out of here.
I'm not sure we can just cut them, Mr. Carey. They're very well protected.
Oh, that was a waste of time, then. Let's get back before we're missed and the Doctor...
Do not move. You are my prisoners. Resistance is useless.
Oh, yeah, chum. Try catching us for...
My arm! You can crush my arm!
It will be replaced. You will both come with me.
Where are you taking us?
Controller, I have brought the humans.
Excellent. I have to damage this one.
No matter. Take it to the conversion chamber.
We haven't time to create a completely new Cyberman.
But reprogram his brain. It plants new auditory and visual circuits and replace his arm.
No! No, what are you doing?
Mr. Carey, I haven't...
Silence. You are the Doctor's companion.
I prefer to think that he's mine, actually.
You will be attached to our conversion process.
You mean I'm going to become one of you?
No. Your body has no purpose, but your mind.
That will become like us. Like me.
Your brain will be reprogrammed and then placed within the operational controls of the Doctor's TARDIS.
You will pilot it for us.
You will be an extension of both the craft and cyber technology.
You will be a Cyber Controller.
